text:
Alex: Heads-up — NF4 canary (canary-3) shows a sharp memory prefill spike after yesterday's calibration heuristic change. Throughput down ~28% on p99 workloads :warning:
Jen: :eyes: which change specifically? the new prefill threshold or the recalibrated scale-table?
Alex: scale-table tweak + aggressive prefill for short-prefix optimization. We see prefill go from ~200MB -> ~1.4GB on worker-7.
Ravi: Can you paste the `nvidia-smi` snapshot and the runtime logs?
Alex: pasted below:
```
GPU 0: 40%  12GB / 16GB
GPU 1: 95% 15.4GB / 16GB  # worker-7
Process 12345  inference_server  14.9GB
```
logs snippet:
```
[2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] kernel_selector: chosen=quant4_nf4_prefill_v2
[2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] cache_manager: prefill_estimate=1.4GB prefix_len=96
[2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] batcher: microbatch=8 -> flush
[2026-02-12T14:03:22Z] perf: tail_lat=420ms throughput_drop=28%
```
Mike: Interesting — the new kernel `quant4_nf4_prefill_v2` has different KV layout assumptions. If prefill is overestimated it may keep large slabs pinned.
Jen: Could be interacting with the slab allocator heuristics. We recently increased slab coalescing to avoid fragmentation. That plus bigger prefill -> less free slab for new KV pages.
Ravi: Can we repro on a small canary? Steps?
Alex: repro steps: run `canary-run --model=xlarge-nf4 --profile=p99 --scale-table=v2` for 30m. You'll see progressive growth as more prefixes are cached.
Jen: I'll run that now on canary-5 with `--slab-coalesce=off` to isolate.
perf-bot: perf alert created: perf/2467894321 - NF4 canary 3 memory spike. Linked traces: https://perf.redwood/trace/2467894321
Mike: Also check kernel selection logs: maybe fallback path triggers `int8_slowpath` for certain layers, causing memory churn.
Alex: Good call — I see lines later in log: `kernel: layer-22 -> fallback=int8_slowpath` around the same time.
Ravi: If fallback happens mid-request, we might be duplicating KV contexts (old + new) until GC runs. That would explain transient spike + throughput drop.
Jen: Repro on canary-5 with coalesce off shows smaller spike (~500MB) and throughput only -8%. Starting a trace now.
Alex: Can we try a quick rollback of the scale-table only? If that's the culprit we can hotfix without touching allocator.
Mike: Rollback plan: 1) pin canary to `scale-table=v1` 2) set `kernel_selector.force=quant4_nf4_prefill_v1` 3) monitor for 15m.
Ravi: If that fixes it, follow-up: add a guard in selector to avoid prefill when slab_free < X MB.
Jen: Trace update: saw fallback -> slowpath at layer 18 caused a host copy. stack shows repeated `kv_cache_alloc` attempts and `slab_wait` events.
Alex: Kicking the rollback now on canary-3.
perf-bot: rollout action recorded: rollback scale-table -> v1 on canary-3 by Alex at 14:28:43Z
sre-bot: alert suppressed for perf/2467894321 while investigating (30m).
Jen: After rollback: memory stabilized ~220MB prefill and throughput returned to baseline. p99 tail back to normal.
Ravi: Happy path confirmed. Next steps: 1) Add prefill sanity check in runtime (min free slab threshold) 2) Update kernel docs to clearly document KV layout expectations 3) Run a small automated stress test to catch this interaction earlier.
Mike: I'll own the runtime guard (1). Jen pls run stress harness for (3). Alex/Ravi prepare a short postmortem with timings.
Alex: Will draft PM and include profiling traces, kernel selection logs, and repro script.
Jen: Added task to infra: `INFRA-872` - add slab-free telemetry to canary dashboards.
Ravi: Also let's add a perf regression gate for new kernel variants that runs on long-prefix workloads to catch prefill blowups earlier.
Alex: Thanks all. If anyone sees related anomalies on prod, ping me and we'll escalate. :thumbsup:
